title: Double Pointers (int **)
concept: A double pointer stores a pointer's address and accesses the original value through an extra level of indirection

steps.title: Starting main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

Next we build the reference chain `a -> p -> pp`.

steps.title: 1. Declaring an integer variable
steps.explanation:
`int a = 10;` prepares the original integer value.

This variable is the final target of the pointer chain.

steps.title: 2. Declaring a single pointer
steps.explanation:
`p` stores the address of `a`, making it point to `a`.

`p` is a variable that holds location information, not the value itself.

steps.title: 3. Declaring a double pointer
steps.explanation:
`pp` stores the address of `p`, making it point to a pointer.

This completes the two-level chain: `pp -> p -> a`.

steps.title: Printing the initial value
steps.explanation: We print `a` before modification to establish a baseline for comparison.

steps.title: Changing a value through double dereference
steps.explanation:
`**pp = 20;` follows the chain to change the final target `a`.

The intermediate addresses (values of `p` and `pp`) remain unchanged -- only the original data is modified.
steps.keyInsight: `**pp` follows the pointer chain to reach the final original data.

steps.title: Verifying the changed value
steps.explanation: Printing again confirms that `a` has changed to 20.

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation:
The program ends with `return 0;`.

Key point: Double pointers are useful when you need to indirectly control a pointer itself.

quiz.question: Given int val = 5; int *p = &val; int **pp = &p; which does NOT read the value of val?
quiz.explanation:
&p is the address of pointer p (the value of pp), so it is not 5.
val == *p == **pp.

misconceptions.wrong: A pointer to a pointer is a special hardware feature.
misconceptions.correct: It is simply a variable holding the address of a variable that holds an address.
misconceptions.why: From a memory perspective, all pointers are integer variables of the same size (32/64 bit).

keyTakeaway: A double pointer is used when you want to change a pointer variable's value through a reference.
